h1: Baan I Inspire — a teak boutique B&B in Nai Wiang, Phrae, where service feels like being a houseguest
intro: Picture this: a three-storey house scented with teak, set in the Nai Wiang area of Phrae town, where the owner comes out to greet you with a smile and tips on what to eat and where to go today — Baan I Inspire is a 22-room boutique B&B on Ratuthit Road that uses teak and local materials throughout, built on a simple, eco-minded idea · what real reviews agree on is the warm service from the English-speaking owner, the homemade breakfast, and the location just about 5 minutes from Phrae Airport · there's a free airport shuttle, free parking, and bikes to rent for exploring the old town · from about ฿1,015/night · ranked #3 of 14 B&B-type stays in Phrae on TripAdvisor, scoring 4.6 out of 5

body.html: Who Baan I Inspire is for — to put it as simply as possible, Baan I Inspire is for people who want "a small house with someone looking after you" rather than a hotel where everything runs on autopilot · this isn't a luxury resort, there's no rooftop pool, and it doesn't sell grandeur, but it's a 22-room boutique B&B that has been open since October 2015 in the Nai Wiang area of Mueang Phrae district · what gets people talking is the homey atmosphere, plus the care of an owner who comes down to chat with guests personally, speaks fluent English, and helps recommend where to eat and what to see · from real reviews on TripAdvisor, Agoda and Booking.com, the people who fit best here are couples, solo travellers, foreign visitors who like local stays, and road trippers exploring the north who care about cleanliness, genuine service, and an easy base for the old town more than about ticking off every amenity a big hotel has · on the flip side, anyone set on a stay with a pool, a gym, or round-the-clock chain-hotel service may find this place too pared-back · TripAdvisor ranks Baan I Inspire #3 of 14 B&B/Inn-type stays in Phrae with a score of 4.6 out of 5, which is very high for a small stay in a secondary city and confirms that it is genuinely still open today

Location and getting around — Baan I Inspire sits at 60/1 Ratuthit Road, Nai Wiang subdistrict, Mueang Phrae district, a spot that works well for anyone who wants to stay inside the old town but off the busy main roads · what foreign reviews mention most is that the stay is only about 1.3 km from Phrae Airport (PRH), or roughly a 5-minute drive, so anyone flying into Phrae reaches the property almost immediately, and there's a free airport shuttle too, which helps a lot since public transport is harder to find here than in bigger cities · from the stay it's about 4–6 minutes into the old town and the main sights · Khum Chao Luang Phrae and Ban Wongburi (the antique teak houses that are icons of the town) are about 1.5–2 km away, while Wat Phra That Cho Hae, the province's most important shrine, is about 8–9 km away, or a 15-minute drive · for anyone who likes shopping for mor hom indigo cloth, Thung Hong village is not far to the north, a short drive away · one honest note: Ratuthit Road is in a residential area with little passing public transport, so if you're not driving yourself, having your own car or renting a motorbike/bicycle makes getting around much easier · the good news is the stay has bikes to rent, ideal for riding around the quiet old town

"Flew into Phrae in the evening, called the stay, and the owner drove out to pick us up at the airport — we were at the house in under ten minutes · the room was clean, the teak smelled lovely, and in the morning we had a breakfast the owner cooked herself; it felt as warm as staying with relatives."

Room types and decor — Baan I Inspire has 22 rooms across a three-storey building, in several sizes to suit both couples and families · the entry-level room is the S Room at about 24 sqm with an added daybed, stepping up to the M Room at about 38 sqm with a teak work desk, good for people who work as they go or want a more open room, and the largest is the L Room at about 47 sqm, a one-bedroom suite with a separate living area, suited to families or anyone who wants more space · what every room shares is decor in teak and local materials, true to the stay's concept of using local items and emphasising sustainability, giving a warm, natural feel rather than a cookie-cutter hotel room · all rooms have air-conditioning, an en-suite bathroom with a shower, free Wi-Fi, and some have a private balcony · many reviews praise the rooms as more spacious than expected for the price, and very clean · one thing to know first is that several reviews mention the beds are fairly firm by Thai bed standards, which some people like because their back feels good, but others used to soft beds may need to adjust · if mattress firmness matters to you, it's worth asking and requesting an extra pillow or topper at check-in

Facilities — to be upfront first, Baan I Inspire is a small B&B-style stay, so there's no pool or gym · if you're after a rooftop pool or a full spa, this isn't the answer, and you should look at a higher-tier hotel in town instead · but for what you actually need to explore Phrae, it has the essentials covered in a small-stay way · the highlight is the free airport shuttle, which matters a lot in a town with limited public transport · there's free private parking (though the space is fairly limited given the size of the stay, so it's best not to arrive too late when it's full) · there are bikes to rent for riding around the old town, an activity that suits Phrae's quiet streets · on top of that there's massage service, a tour information desk, laundry service, daily housekeeping, and 24-hour check-in · free high-speed Wi-Fi covers the whole property · the teak-decorated common area is a place to sit and relax, and many guests say it's where they got to chat casually with the owner and other guests, a charm unique to this style of stay

Food and breakfast — breakfast is included in the room rate and is another point that draws consistent praise in real reviews · it's not a big chain-hotel buffet but a freshly made homemade breakfast that many foreign reviews call "excellent," especially the Thai-style breakfast · one story from a review captures the owner's care well: a guest was vegetarian, and the owner went out to buy ingredients specifically to cook them a vegetarian breakfast — a detail that's rare at this price point · for other meals, the Nai Wiang location helps a lot, since a short drive or bike ride reaches the restaurants and cafés in the old town, including the Kad Kong Kao walking street that runs on Saturdays only · the owner often recommends the town's good local spots, so many guests get to try local food that isn't in the guidebooks · overall, food at Baan I Inspire isn't about luxury or a huge selection but about freshness, hands-on cooking, and care like you'd get from someone you know, which fits the stay's overall character

Service — this is the heart and the number-one selling point of Baan I Inspire, no question · real reviews from nearly every source agree that the owner and team are very friendly and attentive · the owner speaks fluent English, which puts foreign travellers at ease in a town where not many speak it, and often shares tips on what to see and eat, driving routes, and the best timing for each place · many people say it feels more like having a local friend than just hotel staff · the airport shuttle, help with little things, and flexibility in looking after each guest are what earn this place a score well above its size · to be fair, because it's a small, family-run stay, service at times may not be as formal or fast as a hotel with several shifts of staff, but on sincerity and warmth, almost no one has a complaint

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulled together from TripAdvisor, Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com, and the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the warm service from the English-speaking owner who helps with everything, the homemade breakfast that many call better than expected, rooms that are clean and bigger than the price suggests, the warm teak decor with a real local feel, the location near the airport and easy access to the old town, and the free airport shuttle that genuinely helps · On the gripe side: the most frequently mentioned point is fairly firm beds by Thai bed standards, which comes down to personal preference · next is the air-conditioner compressor noise in some rooms, which is fairly loud, to the point that some reviews suggest packing earplugs, plus roosters crowing in the early morning since it's in an area that still has traditional homes, and the fact that some sights and restaurants aren't within walking distance and need a car or bike · most of these gripes are typical of a small stay in a secondary city rather than problems that keep guests from returning, and many still give high scores even while mentioning them

"Lovely, clean stay, the owner is so kind and recommended places to eat and visit the whole time · the only downside was the bed was a touch too firm for us, and the first night the air-con was a bit loud, but once we asked to move bed position and adjust the air-con it got better; great value for Phrae."

Price and value — Baan I Inspire's starting price is about ฿1,015–1,300/night for a standard twin room in the normal price range, rising with room size for the M Room and L Room (suite) · compared with other stays in Phrae, this sits in the town's mid-range — higher than pure guesthouses and hostels but lower than larger hotels with a pool · what makes it feel worth it is that you're not just paying for the room but getting a free airport shuttle, homemade breakfast, the personal care of an English-speaking owner, and rooms bigger than the price suggests · for foreign travellers visiting Phrae for the first time who want a stay they can "rely on" for information and getting around, the value here is in the peace of mind more than the numbers · but if your goal is the cheapest price possible, or you want the full set of amenities a big hotel has, there are other options in Phrae that fit a budget or amenities more closely

Good to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, if you're flying into Phrae, give your flight time in advance to use the free airport shuttle; it's far easier than finding your own ride · two, if you're a light sleeper or don't like firm beds, say so when you book — ask for a quiet room and check on the mattress, and you can request an extra pillow or topper · three, pack earplugs just in case if you're sensitive to air-con noise or early-morning roosters · four, if you're not driving yourself, plan how you'll get around town in advance, such as renting the stay's bikes or a motorbike, since public transport in Phrae is limited · five, during festivals and long holidays the stay has limited rooms, so book ahead and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm · six, ask the owner about your travel plans, because the local tips you get often make a Phrae trip more fun than what you planned yourself

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Baan I Inspire is the best fit for people who want a clean, friendly boutique B&B with warm service in the Nai Wiang area of Phrae, near the airport, and want a local to help with travel tips · the teak and local materials, homemade breakfast, free airport shuttle, and English-speaking owner make it a good base for exploring Phrae, especially for foreign travellers and couples who prefer local stays over chain hotels · if you're after a pool, a gym, a stay within walking distance of every meal, or the plush beds of a five-star hotel, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a larger hotel in town instead · but for a Phrae trip where you want sincerity, cleanliness, and a location that works — Baan I Inspire is a worthwhile, reassuring choice, which is why it has consistently scored high and ranked among the top B&B-type stays in Phrae

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Baan I Inspire Phrae

faq.q: Where is Baan I Inspire, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's located at 60/1 Ratuthit Road, Nai Wiang subdistrict, Mueang Phrae district, in the old town · it's only about 1.3 km from Phrae Airport (PRH), or a 5-minute drive, with a free airport shuttle · the main sights like Khum Chao Luang and Ban Wongburi are about 5 minutes away · Wat Phra That Cho Hae is about a 15-minute drive away

faq.q: How much does Baan I Inspire cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,015–1,300/night for a standard twin room in the normal price range · there's the S Room (~24 sqm with a daybed), M Room (~38 sqm with a teak work desk), and L Room, a one-bedroom suite (~47 sqm with a separate living area) good for families · prices depend on room size and timing, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Baan I Inspire for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travellers, foreign visitors, and road trippers who want a clean, friendly stay with warm service in the Nai Wiang area of Phrae · it stands out for the English-speaking owner who recommends where to eat and visit, and the location near the airport · it's not a fit for people who want a pool, a gym, or the full set of amenities a big hotel has

faq.q: Does it have breakfast and an airport shuttle?
faq.a: It has both · breakfast is included in the room rate and is freshly made homemade, and many foreign reviews praise it, especially the Thai dishes, and the owner has even gone out to buy ingredients to make a guest a special vegetarian breakfast · there's a free Phrae Airport shuttle, just give your flight time in advance — very handy in a town where public transport is hard to find

faq.q: What should I know before booking Baan I Inspire?
faq.a: The most common notes in reviews are fairly firm beds by Thai bed standards, loud air-con compressor noise in some rooms, and roosters crowing in the early morning · it's a small B&B-style stay with no pool or gym, and some spots need a car · if you sleep lightly, ask for a quiet room, check on the mattress, and pack earplugs just in case

faq.q: If I'm not driving myself, is it easy to explore Phrae from Baan I Inspire?
faq.a: It's reasonably easy if you plan ahead · the stay has bikes to rent for comfortably riding around the quiet old town, and there's a free airport shuttle · but since public transport in Phrae is limited, some restaurants and sights need a car or a rented motorbike · the owner can recommend routes and ways to get around, so ask at check-in
